t: You're standing outside The Old Bank of England, a pub at 194 Fleet Street, right where the City of London meets the City of Westminster. The building was designed by Arthur Blomfield, who really was architect to the Bank of England. He built the bank's Law Courts branch in 1883, and that is the link to this address. He was also a keen church builder, was knighted, and received the RIBA gold medal in 1891.
